thread.title: Senator Anderson criticizes state budget proposal after governor's address
thread.title_full: Senator Anderson criticizes state budget proposal after governor's address

author: P. G. Lennon
title: Senator Anderson criticizes state budget proposal after governor's address
text:
State Senator Neil Anderson, a Republican representing Illinois’ 47th Senate District, issued a response following the Governor’s annual State of the State and Budget Address. Anderson acknowledged support for expanding vocational programs but criticized other aspects of the budget proposal.
“I’m glad the Governor talked about expanding vocational programs. Illinois needs to invest in skilled trades, especially in West Central Illinois. But beyond that, this was the same old Springfield story: more spending, more government, and no serious plan to pay for it. Agriculture, the backbone of my district and the top economic driver in Illinois, was not even mentioned. While the United States economy has surged ahead, Illinois keeps falling behind because of high taxes and reckless spending. This budget is nearly a billion dollars out of balance unless they raise taxes again, and taxpayers cannot afford it,” Anderson said.
Anderson has served as state senator since his election in 2023 to represent the 47th Senate District, succeeding Jil Tracy.
